introP1: Archives are mediators and actors of collective memory, a key element connecting institutions to communities’ past, present, and future. Within contemporary archival discourse and illustrated by case studies, we can see how not only the content of archives in institutions’ collections but also the way in which they are organised and the infrastructures they are under — their context — matter to what narratives are constructed. Colonial, oppressive structures have allowed for the archive to become a space where some stories are told and not others, some names are mentioned, but not all are credited, where cultural practices are made invisible, and places and peoples erased as their presence is unnamed.
introP2: The Asterisk* is a tool that addresses and works on the need for a more thorough, critical, and contextualised way of describing archival items by adding new descriptions and alternative titles, expanding thesaurus, or engaging with the material through alternative methods. The Asterisk* also addresses underexposed collection items, highlighting previously untold stories: the more information is added about a particular object, the more likely it is to be seen by researchers and other publics, thus developing institutions towards increasing accessibility and diversity in Heritage.
missionP1: In bringing archival material into the present, re-appropriating digital infrastructures or ways of situating the archive are therefore essential as we move towards a post/de/colonial collection. Bringing urgency to the question of how one archives, the Asterisk* is not only a way to engage, but a practical tool that can be taken outside of the het Nieuwe Insituut’s and collection, used by other institutions, community archives, or researchers. In an inclusive digital space, making asterisks is imperative to a collection that is both ever-present and ever-changing.
missionP2: Nieuwe Instituut is working towards describing collection material and advise on registration guidelines for future and critical approaches to archival descriptions and metadata. At the same time, the Asterisk* will approach the collection both artistically and experimentally, through featured “Stories” on the Collection Platform. Ultimately, the main goal of the Asterisk* is to contribute to a better contextualised, societally relevant, and accessible collection.
